findings.title: SkillsMachine has two overlapping sources of project instructions
findings.technical_title: WHOAMI competes with HUMAN as semantic home
findings.fact: Useful project context exists in WHOAMI while HUMAN is intended to be the canonical semantic home.
findings.inference: Keeping both as instruction sources can create ambiguity inside SkillsMachine.
findings.summary: Keeping both as instruction sources can create ambiguity inside SkillsMachine.

evidence.label: DEC-W4-047
evidence.excerpt: HUMAN must become the semantic home of useful WHOAMI context/data; WHOAMI must not remain competing semantic canon.

evidence.label: Q-064
evidence.excerpt: SkillsMachine evaluates and implements locally after consulting its HUMAN and Q&A; Wings4 does not mutate SkillsMachine.

evidence.label: Transfer package
evidence.excerpt: STATUS ready for SkillsMachine ORCHESTRATOR review; THIS_IS_NOT_AN_EXECUTOR_PROMPT=YES.

findings.impact: If unresolved, people and AI sessions may follow competing project instructions and weaken a single source of authority.
alternatives: A. Retire WHOAMI after checking dependencies
B. Reduce WHOAMI to a short pointer to HUMAN
C. Keep WHOAMI temporarily with an explicit deprecation notice
findings.recommendation: Send the prepared transfer to SkillsMachine; prefer a short WHOAMI pointer to HUMAN if local dependencies allow; require return evidence before treating the work as verified. Independent project re-check is not yet available.
findings.decision_options_note: Visible POSTPONE replaces DEFER; internal legacy DEFER/DEFERRED mapping remains acceptable.

evidence.label: Active BATON

evidence.label: Q-064 / compiled interpretation
evidence.excerpt: Unrelated SkillsMachine dirty workstreams remain out of scope.

findings.impact: Mixing unrelated unfinished work risks wrong attribution, accidental combined commits and delayed readiness.

Freeze the SMDI candidate until a separate review
Postpone unrelated work while the WHOAMI→HUMAN transfer proceeds alone
findings.recommendation: Keep unrelated unfinished work out of the WHOAMI transfer. Require SkillsMachine-local disposition before any local execution authorization.
findings.decision_options_note: Visible POSTPONE replaces DEFER; internal legacy DEFER/DEFERRED mapping remains acceptable.

findings.title: Market Check results cannot be exported as a management note
findings.technical_title: No bounded Market Check result export on the operator surface
findings.fact: The operator can run Market Check on demand and read the result on screen. Copy/download exist for intervention packages, not for the Market Check result record.
findings.inference: If gerencia needs a portable note, Wings still has a remaining local gap. That gap is not a reason to buy a market-intelligence product.
findings.summary: Market Check is callable, but the result stays on screen. A small Wings-local export would close a remaining custom gap.

evidence.label: Operator surface
evidence.excerpt: DOWNLOAD INTERVENTION PACKAGE / COPY PACKAGE exist; Market Check persists only in local demo state.

findings.impact: Operators cannot hand a Market Check result to gerencia without copy-paste from the screen.
alternatives: A. Build a bounded result note/export in Wings
C. Wait for a named external tool comparison (not evidenced)
findings.recommendation: Build only the remaining Market Check result-note gap inside Wings. Do not invent a market product.
findings.decision_options_note: Visible POSTPONE replaces DEFER; internal legacy DEFER/DEFERRED mapping remains acceptable.

findings.title: Optional Skills/GRC product integration is recorded but not implemented
findings.technical_title: DEC-W4-053 integration relationship has no live integration slice
findings.fact: DEC-W4-053 records that Wings may optionally integrate with SkillsMachine for reusable Skills/GRC. That integration is not mandatory and is not implemented as a live product slice.
findings.inference: The first evidenced class is integration of an existing provider, not building a second Skills/GRC platform, and not monitoring the market.
findings.summary: Wings already named an optional Skills/GRC integration. No same-project implementation exists. Child-project mutation remains prohibited.

evidence.label: DEC-W4-053
evidence.excerpt: As products: Wings4 may optionally integrate with SkillsMachine for reusable Skills/GRC; that integration is not mandatory.

findings.impact: Without a bounded integration slice, operators cannot use Skills/GRC from Wings except by leaving the current diagnostic.
alternatives: A. Integrate SkillsMachine as an optional Skills/GRC service
B. Build a second Skills/GRC platform in Wings (not evidenced)
C. Leave the relationship recorded and unimplemented
findings.recommendation: Prefer governed integration of the existing SkillsMachine Skills/GRC provider. Do not mutate SkillsMachine from Wings. Do not start market monitoring.
findings.decision_options_note: Visible POSTPONE replaces DEFER; internal legacy DEFER/DEFERRED mapping remains acceptable.
